speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you describe exactly what happens during these episodes of unresponsiveness and facial grimacing? Specifically, do you lose awareness completely, and how long do these episodes typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the patient have any history of head trauma or seizures in the family, and does he experience any other symptoms like headaches or vision changes? I will also request an EEG to evaluate for seizure activity. REQUEST TEST: EEG

text: The EEG findings, combined with the olfactory aura and automatisms, strongly suggest focal seizures originating in the temporal lobe. To identify the underlying structural cause, I will request further imaging. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRI and EEG findings, this is likely idiopathic temporal lobe epilepsy. Do the episodes occur more frequently at night or upon waking, and have you noticed any triggers like stress or lack of sleep?

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient's symptoms, including the olfactory aura, automatisms, and post-ictal confusion, along with temporal lobe spikes on EEG, are classic for temporal lobe epilepsy. Since the MRI is normal, this confirms a diagnosis of idiopathic focal epilepsy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
